Free resources

Tools for a calmer gut, on their way.

I’m putting together free resources you can use between appointments, or before you’re ready to book. Choose the ones you’d like and I’ll email you as soon as each one is ready.

  • AudioMP3 · about 10 minutes

    A 10-minute gut-calming relaxation

    A short guided relaxation to help settle your nervous system when your gut flares. Listen with headphones, somewhere you can sit or lie down.

    Coming soon

  • PrintablePDF · printable

    Gut-brain symptom diary

    A simple daily page for noticing patterns between your symptoms, stress, sleep and meals, so you have something concrete to bring to your GP or to our sessions.

    Coming soon

  • GuidePDF guide

    The gut-brain connection, in plain English

    How your gut and brain talk to each other, why stress and symptoms feed each other, and what gut-directed therapy actually involves.

    Coming soon

  • ChecklistPDF · one page

    Questions to ask your GP about IBS

    A one-page checklist to help you get the most from your next appointment, including the questions people often wish they’d asked.

Jay Hayes Gut-brain therapy

Psychotherapy and gut-directed hypnotherapy for people living with IBS and other gut-brain conditions. Sessions online, from Brisbane.

A note on medical care. Gut-brain therapy works alongside medical care, not instead of it. If you haven’t already, please see your GP or gastroenterologist to rule out other causes of your symptoms. If you’re in crisis, call Lifeline on 13 11 14 or emergency services on 000.

Jay lives and works on the lands of the Turrbal and Yuggera peoples. She pays her respects to Elders past and present, and acknowledges Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples as the Traditional Custodians of this land.
